# @dschz/solid-flow — agent cheatsheet

SolidJS port of React Flow / Svelte Flow (node-based UIs). Built for SolidJS 2.0
(solid-js@2.0.0-rc.x, install with the `next` tag). Same gesture engine as
upstream (@xyflow/system), different state model. This file front-loads what an
agent trained on React Flow will get wrong here.

## If you know React Flow, unlearn these

- NO `onNodesChange` / `onEdgesChange` / `applyNodeChanges` / `applyEdgeChanges`.
  They do not exist and are not needed. State is store-based: mutate your store
  and the flow follows.
- NO `useReactFlow` — it is `useSolidFlow()`, and it must be called INSIDE
  `<SolidFlow>` (or under `<SolidFlowProvider>`). Returns `{ flow, commands }`
  plus commands spread at the top level. `flow` is the read surface
  (`flow.nodes`, `flow.edges`, `flow.selection`, `flow.viewport`),
  `commands` the write surface (`addNodes`, `updateNode`, `setViewport`,
  `fitView`, `deleteElements`, `toObject`, ...).
- Mouse-named events are pointer-named here: `onNodePointerEnter` /
  `onNodePointerMove` / `onNodePointerLeave` (same for edges and the pane),
  NOT `onNodeMouseEnter`. Double-clicks, `onPaneScroll`, and
  `onViewportChange` exist with React Flow semantics.
- Styles: `import "@dschz/solid-flow/styles"` once, or nothing renders sensibly.
- Components run ONCE (Solid). No re-renders, no dependency arrays, no memo
  ceremony. Read reactive values in JSX/computations, not in component-body
  statements.

## State model (the core contract)

Two modes, per axis (nodes and edges independently):

- CONTROLLED (`nodes={...}` / `edges={...}`): your store owns membership.
  Draft-mutate for O(changed) updates; wholesale replacement re-seeds (rows
  keyed by id). The flow writes runtime fields (position on drag, `selected`,
  `measured`) onto your rows. Imperative commands do NOT write membership back
  to your store — adopt new elements yourself (see onConnect below).
- UNCONTROLLED (`defaultNodes` / `defaultEdges`): seeds ONCE; the flow owns
  membership afterwards. Commands and completed connections write membership
  directly. Later changes to the default props are ignored by contract.

```tsx
import { createEdgeStore, createNodeStore, SolidFlow } from "@dschz/solid-flow";
import "@dschz/solid-flow/styles";

const [nodes, setNodes] = createNodeStore([
  { id: "1", type: "input", data: { label: "In" }, position: { x: 250, y: 0 } },
  { id: "2", data: { label: "Mid" }, position: { x: 100, y: 100 } },
]);
const [edges, setEdges] = createEdgeStore([{ id: "e1-2", source: "1", target: "2" }]);

// Controlled: adopt completed connections into YOUR store.
const onConnect = (c) => setEdges((draft) => { draft.push(c); });

<SolidFlow nodes={nodes} edges={edges} onConnect={onConnect} fitView>
  <Background variant="dots" /> <Controls /> <MiniMap />
</SolidFlow>
```

Custom nodes: register components in `nodeTypes`; each element's `data` type is
narrowed by its `type` field (`createNodeStore<typeof nodeTypes>([...])`).
Custom node components receive `NodeProps` and render `<Handle type="source"
position={Position.Bottom} />` for connectivity.

## Async and persistence (SolidJS 2.0 rules)

- Loading from a server: `createNodeStore(async () => fetchNodes())` — no memo,
  no lifecycle. Reads are not-ready until the data lands; wrap with
  `<Loading fallback={...}>` from @solidjs/web (or don't — the canvas renders
  and the graph pops in). Works for controlled props AND defaults.
- NEVER wrap flow-store reads in broad try/catch in your own computations: a
  not-ready read throws `NotReadyError`, and that propagation is load-bearing
  (it is the server build's only re-derive channel). Branch with `isPending()`.
- Saving to a server — use draft-then-commit, NOT per-mutation sync:

```tsx
const [serverGraph] = createStore(() => api.loadGraph(), { nodes: [], edges: [] });
// seed once from server truth; the flow owns the draft:
<SolidFlow defaultNodes={serverGraph.nodes} defaultEdges={serverGraph.edges}>
// one action batch-commits the whole draft:
const save = action(function* () {
  yield api.saveGraph(commands.toObject());
  refresh(serverGraph);
});
```

  A failed save keeps the draft (retry-friendly); the refresh cannot clobber
  edits.
- DO NOT pass a `createOptimisticStore` as `nodes`/`edges`. Flow-internal
  writes (selection, drag) would land on the optimistic overlay outside any
  action and revert silently. Use draft-then-commit above.

## Commands quick reference

`fitView`, `fitBounds`, `zoomIn/Out`, `setZoom`, `setCenter`, `setViewport`,
`panBy`, `screenToFlowPosition`, `flowToScreenPosition`, `addNodes`, `addEdges`,
`setNodes`, `setEdges`, `updateNode`, `updateNodeData`, `updateEdge`,
`deleteElements`, `getIntersectingNodes`, `isNodeIntersecting`,
`getNodesBounds`, `updateNodeInternals`, `toObject`.

Element hooks: `useNode(id)`, `useEdge(id)`, `useNodes()`, `useEdges()`,
`useSelectedNodes()`, `useSelectedEdges()`, `useNodeConnections()`,
`useKeyPress(keys)` — all Accessor-based.

## Misc gotchas

- Give nodes explicit `width`/`height` for SSR (no DOM to measure) and for
  meaningful first paint.
- Viewport culling is ON by default (CSS tier); `onlyRenderVisibleElements`
  unmounts off-screen elements; opt out per element with `cullable: false`.
- Keep `solid-js` and `@solidjs/web` on the same 2.0.0-rc.x version.
- Edge reconnection: `<EdgeReconnectAnchor>` inside custom edges;
  `onReconnect` + `reconnectEdge` utility.
- Full docs: README.md in this package; examples: playground/ in the repo
  (https://github.com/dsnchz/solid-flow).
